sections.h2: Which Trumbull County office does what with my tax bill?
sections.html:
Two courthouse-square offices split the work from the second floor of the Administration Building at 160 High Street NW in Warren. The Auditor sets values, takes homestead applications and receives Board of Revision complaints. The Treasurer prints the bills and collects the money.

  • Auditor: 330-675-2420, or 330-675-2895 for questions about a specific valuation.
  • Treasurer: 330-675-2436, with no lunchtime closing, per its FAQ.
  • Board of Revision filings by email: BOR@co.trumbull.oh.us.

Rate cards for each taxing district, back to 2010, are linked from the Treasurer's tax information page. Bills, payment history and values live in the Auditor's online property search, except manufactured homes, which are not listed there and need a call to the Treasurer.

sections.h2: What sets Trumbull County apart for a house seller?
sections.html:
Trumbull fills the far northeast corner of Ohio with a square outline about 25 miles across, a shape Wikipedia says no other Ohio county shares. Established in 1800, it once held the entire Connecticut Western Reserve, and Warren began as that territory's capital. Today Warren is the seat. Cortland, Girard, Hubbard and Niles are the other cities, a slice of Youngstown extends in from the south, and I-80, US 62, US 422 and State Route 11 carry the traffic.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table estimates 198,972 people for 2025, a 1.5 percent slide since 2020, in 94,514 housing units. Owners hold 71.3 percent of occupied homes. The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $141,800 for 2020 to 2024, the median rent is $797 and median household income is $56,435. Nearly a quarter of residents, 24.3 percent, are 65 or older, so the age-based homestead exemption touches many sellers. Permit activity is light, with 112 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: When does Trumbull County collect, and where do I pay?
sections.html:
Collections come twice a year, usually around March and August, with the exact days printed on each bill. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026 the Treasurer posted March 6 and August 31, 2026, and manufactured homes ran March 2 and August 21, 2026. Bills tend to go out by the end of January and again by the end of June. Early payment earns no discount.

Payment choices on the Treasurer's pages:

  • Mail a check or money order to the Treasurer, 160 High Street NW, Floor 2A, Warren, OH 44481. The postmark date is honored.
  • Drop it in the box on Harmon Avenue beside the building's side steps, open around the clock for checks and money orders.
  • Go online through the Auditor's property search and its Tax tab, using an e-check, debit card or credit card.
  • Pay at the counter with cash, check, card or money order.

A processing company charges $1.00 per e-check and 2.5 percent of the total on cards, and the county gets none of it. A returned check costs $15.00. One check may cover several parcels if the parcel numbers are on the memo line. Allow 7 to 10 days after a collection closes for payments to post.

Owners with nothing past due can enroll in the Tax Installment Payment Plan, which prepays through monthly coupons. Ask the Treasurer for a TIP clerk.

sections.h2: How does the Trumbull County Auditor decide what my house is worth?
sections.html:
The Auditor describes a mass appraisal for roughly 144,000 parcels: one method, common data, statistical testing. Inputs include field verification, aerial photos, owner-sent settlement statements or appraisals, auction results and listing-service data. Staff generally cannot enter your home, which is a main reason a single bank appraisal can differ. The county compares three years of sales, and the work takes about two and a half years.

The assessed share is 35 percent of market value. The Auditor's guide to the 2023 reappraisal says Ohio requires a countywide update every three years and that rates then adjust so voted levies raise the same money as before. Only inside millage, 10 mills at most, floats with value. Special assessments for ditches, paving, curbs, sewer and water lines, lighting and trash removal share the bill but are separate from tax.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Trumbull County valuation?
sections.html:
Go through the Board of Revision, which weighs value and never the tax dollars. State law, R.C. 5715.19, closes the window on March 31 or when first-half collection ends, whichever is later. The person complaining has to prove the case.

Trumbull County Board of Revision, from the Auditor's board page
StageWhat happens
MembersAuditor, Treasurer and Commissioners, each free to send a stand-in
FormsDTE 1, 1M or 2 for value; DTE 106B for homestead or owner-occupancy disputes
DeliveryEmail, mail, fax or in person; a handwritten form needs a notary, an electronic one does not
First lookSome files draw a proposed value that you can take or turn down
Hearing noticeAt least 10 days before, in person, by phone or on Webex
EvidenceBest sent with the complaint, and no later than 7 days ahead
Next level30 days from the decision letter to the Board of Tax Appeals or Common Pleas

The board lists an independent appraisal, photos, repair estimates, and a settlement statement with the purchase agreement as common evidence. A school board can counter-file within 30 days. The Auditor warns that taxes stay due during a complaint and that paying in full prevents penalty trouble, with any reduction returned as a credit or refund.

sections.h2: Which Trumbull County reductions can help a seller or heir?
sections.html:
The Auditor's homestead page explains three:

  • Homestead exemption: up to $29,000 off market value. Owners must be 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, or a surviving spouse who was 59 or older when a recipient died. The income cap is $41,000 for 2026 taxes payable in 2027, and $40,000 for a late application on 2025 taxes payable in 2026, using Ohio adjusted gross income for owner and spouse.
  • Disabled veteran exemption: up to $58,000 for veterans rated 100 percent permanently disabled from service, with no income cap.
  • Owner-occupancy reduction: close to 2.5 percent off the bill while the owner lives there, with no filing deadline. It covers the home and one acre.

Appeal a denial on form DTE 106B within 60 days of the notice. Manufactured home owners have until January 31 of the next year. Separately, form DTE 23A asks for remission of a late-payment penalty. The taxpayer files it with the Treasurer, and the board reviews it when the Auditor cannot grant it.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Trumbull County house changes hands?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's FAQ says the owner of record when a bill comes due is responsible, and each bill carries the deeded owner as of the start of the tax year. Sellers and buyers should read their purchase agreement for who reimburses whom. The Treasurer does not keep that agreement, so a title or mortgage company is the place to ask.

At the Auditor's conveyance desk, a transfer costs $4.00 per thousand of value plus $0.50 per parcel, and an exempt transfer costs only the parcel charge. A deed travels to the Tax Map office, then the Auditor, then the Recorder, with a clear copy of the last deed of record. By mail, add a stamped return envelope and a check to the Trumbull County Auditors Office.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes on a Trumbull County house?
sections.html:
Tax foreclosure sales are held in person every other Thursday at 1:30 p.m. in the Commissioners' hearing room, under rules effective May 7, 2026. Bidding starts at a minimum and rises by $100. The top bidder leaves $3,000 in certified funds and owes the balance 30 days after the sale is confirmed. The owner can redeem until the judge signs that confirmation. Bank mortgage foreclosures have moved to an online site under House Bill 390.

The Trumbull County Land Bank, formed in late 2010 through the Treasurer's office, acquires vacant, tax-delinquent parcels and markets them for reuse, working with Trumbull Neighborhood Partnership. If you would rather sell before things reach that point, ask the title company to request a payoff amount from the Treasurer.

faqs.q: Does Trumbull County count the postmark on a mailed payment?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer honors the postmark date on mailed payments, though posting can take 7 to 10 days after a collection closes.

faqs.q: Can I get a discount for paying the whole Trumbull County bill early?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer's FAQ says early full payment earns nothing. Owners who are current can use the monthly coupon plan instead.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax if I sell in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: The owner of record when the bill is due owes it. Your purchase agreement sets who reimburses whom, so read it or ask the title company.

faqs.q: What if the Auditor denies my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File form DTE 106B with the Board of Revision within 60 days of the denial notice. Manufactured home owners have until January 31 of the following year.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for paying by card?
faqs.a: Yes, 2.5 percent of the total, paid to the processing company. E-checks cost $1.00. Cash, checks and money orders avoid the fee.
